thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2365432109 - Multiple CUDA OOMs on prod-gpu-pool-7 (sev=high) -- auto-created channel #incidents. Notifying on-call.

anya: saw the bot. I'm oncall. getting alerts: spike in OOMs across 3 nodes in prod-gpu-pool-7, errors look like allocator failing despite reported headroom.

maria: pulling logs now, adding relevant snippets. logging shows repeated `cudaMalloc` failures but `gpu_free_mem` metric is high (~1.2GB free). suspect fragmentation / reserved-block collisions.

chris: node id: gpu-node-7a2. quick check: `nvidia-smi` shows GPU memory usage 10GB / 24GB but there are many small allocated reserved blocks from spare pool.

anya: timeline: first alert 2365432098, error rate peaked at 2365432103, several containers restarted by k8s OOM killer. customer impact: two customer routes returned 5xx for ~3m.

maria: paste logs:
```
2026-03-15T12:01:03Z runtime ERROR allocation failed: cudaMalloc returned CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
stack: runtime/allocator.cc:482 allocate_chunk
kv_cache reserve list: [id=17 size=256MB state=reserved, id=23 size=128MB state=reserved, id=31 size=64MB state=evicted]
reported_headroom=1.1GB telemetry_headroom=1.05GB
```

chris: interestingly `allocator_report` shows many small free slabs but the largest contiguous free chunk is only ~160MB, so a 256MB reserve can't be satisfied -> OOM even though sum(free)=>1GB.

anya: immediate mitigation proposals?

maria: short-term: disable prefetch/kv-reserve on affected nodes so new allocations avoid large-reserve path. I can push a runtime flag `--kv-reserve-threshold=0` to the daemonset. That should reduce large reserve allocations and let allocator use smaller slabs.

chris: infra side: cordon + drain affected nodes to stop new pods landing on them, then restart GPU drivers on nodes to free any leaked reserved pages. Commands: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-7a2 && kubectl drain gpu-node-7a2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

anya: do that now. Also scale up dedicated spare pool by 1 node to reduce pressure: `k8s autoscaler set min=5` (we're at 4).

maria: rolling patch to runtime config being prepared. quick patch: set `runtime.env: REDWOOD_KV_RESERVE_ENABLED=false` in daemonset, then rollout restart. This will take 45-90s to affect new pods.

chris: driver restart in progress on gpu-node-7a2. kubelet reports pods terminating.

incident-bot: update 2365432118 - Pager duty ack (anya).

anya: customer success pinged customers A & B at 12:04 UTC, told them we see transient 5xx and working on mitigation.

maria: after disabling reserve flag on 2 nodes, we see OOM alarm rate drop to baseline. Telemetry: contiguous_free_chunk increased to ~512MB on restarted nodes.

chris: containers that restarted recovered. one pod (model-service-7) needed manual recreate due to stuck volume mount. that's resolved.

devon: I'm taking the handoff for longer-term investigation. noted the mitigations. next steps: reproduce fragmentation locally with workload replay, instrument allocator to surface contiguous chunk histogram, and propose allocator fallback that splits large reserves into smaller sub-reserves.

anya: good. immediate mitigation summary for postmortem: 1) cordoned/drained affected nodes, restarted drivers, 2) toggled `REDWOOD_KV_RESERVE_ENABLED=false` on runtime daemonset, 3) scaled spare pool by +1 node, 4) CS notified. Impact: ~3m of elevated 5xx for two routes, approx 0.2% of global requests. No data loss.

maria: I opened GH issue runtime#2845 with logs, suggested patch for allocator to attempt compaction/eviction before hard OOM. tagging chris/devon.

incident-bot: incident 2365432109 -> mitigated at 2365432170 (root cause: allocator fragmentation + reserved block sizing). created incident report draft.

devon: I'll lead postmortem/followups. brief to oncall rotation: leave reserve flag off until allocator fallback merged. we'll schedule a canary roll after we have contiguous-chunk histogram metrics.

anya: handing over to devon. I'm available if anything re-escalates. :thumbsup:

sre-pager: acknowledged handoff. adding to weekly triage.
